decisions.reason: The particle therapy water phantom required heavy development investment and supports the firm's high-end therapy QA position, so management will likely attribute its weaker visibility in 2019 to a small, slow-growing particle therapy market rather than drop it.
Small volume chambers are core dosimetry products that rely on the firm's calibration and dosimetry expertise, and they kept their own page in 2019, so there is little reason to abandon them.
This chamber belongs to the firm's central detector portfolio and is used with its phantoms and software, so it reinforces the firm's committed direction.
A multi-model standard clinical chamber line is a foundational, heavily invested product family that is visibly tied to the firm's identity, so removing it is very unlikely.
Relative dosimetry chambers are needed for water phantom scanning workflows, and the firm promotes these integrated workflows, so it will keep the product.
Thimble chambers are staple reference dosimetry devices with long life cycles that are backed by accredited calibration services, so management will continue offering them.
